words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 喂 like the word you’ll use when you pick up the phone — 喂，是田芳吗？
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers open a phone call with 喂. In 课文（一）张东 greets before asking for 田芳.

example.pinyin: Wèi, shì Tián Fāng ma?
example.en: Hello — is that Tian Fang?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 阿姨 like the polite address you’ll use for your friend’s mother — 阿姨，您好！
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers call an older woman 阿姨 even when she isn’t a blood aunt. Here 张东 addresses 田芳妈.

example.zh: 阿姨，您好！田芳去哪儿了？
example.pinyin: Āyí, nín hǎo! Tián Fāng qù nǎr le?
example.en: Auntie, hello! Where has Tian Fang gone?

words.en: a particle used at the end of a sentence to indicate change or the emergence of a new situation
words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added. This lesson’s grammar focus: sentence-final 了 (1).
words.when: Remember 了 like the ending you’ll add when something has happened or a new situation is in — 去哪儿了, 关机了.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers put 了 at the end to affirm occurrence, completion, or change. Pair with 了没有 for yes/no about past events.

example.pinyin: Tián Fāng qù nǎr le?
example.en: Where has Tian Fang gone?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 中学 like the school level before university — 中学同学.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean junior/senior secondary school. Here a 中学同学 is about to go abroad.

example.zh: 她的一个中学同学要出国，她去看看她。
example.pinyin: Tā de yí ge zhōngxué tóngxué yào chūguó, tā qù kànkan tā.
example.en: One of her middle-school classmates is going abroad, so she went to see her.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added. Book prints spaced chū guó.
words.when: Remember 出国 like the word you’ll use when someone leaves the country — 要出国.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 出国 for going overseas (study, work, travel). Related 出 is listed under this entry.

example.zh: 她的一个中学同学要出国，她去看看她。
example.pinyin: Tā de yí ge zhōngxué tóngxué yào chūguó, tā qù kànkan tā.
example.en: One of her middle-school classmates is going abroad, so she went to see her.

words.en: to move from inside to outside
words.note: Listed under the numbered shengci entry in the book (related form). Headword pinyin printed. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 出 like the move-out half of 出国 — from inside a place/country to outside.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 出 as the directional ‘exit’ verb. Here it is the 出 in 出国.

example.zh: 她的一个中学同学要出国。
example.pinyin: Tā de yí ge zhōngxué tóngxué yào chūguó.
example.en: One of her middle-school classmates is going abroad.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added. Book prints 打（电话）.
words.when: Remember 打（电话） like the verb you’ll use for calling someone — 打电话, 打她的手机.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 打电话 / 打手机. Object can be 电话, 手机, or the person.

example.pinyin: Nǐ dǎ tā de shǒujī ba.
example.en: Why don’t you call her mobile.

words.en: to turn off one’s mobile phone
words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 关机 like the word you’ll use when a phone won’t ring — 她关机了.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 关机 for powering off a phone (or ending a PC). Related 关 is under this entry.

example.pinyin: Wǒ dǎ le, kěshì tā guānjī le.
example.en: I called, but her phone was off.

words.en: to turn off; to switch off
words.note: Listed under the numbered shengci entry in the book (related form). Headword pinyin printed. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 关 like the switch-off half of 关机 — turn power off.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 关 lights, machines, phones. Here it is the 关 in 关机.

example.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme guānjī le?
example.en: Why was your phone off?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 饿 like the word you’ll hear when mom urges dinner — 饿了吧？
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 饿了 for ‘I’m hungry.’ 课文（二）田芳妈 greets her with 饿了吧？

example.pinyin: È le ba? Kuài chī fàn ba!
example.en: Hungry, right? Come eat!

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 对了 like the ‘oh right / by the way’ you’ll drop when you suddenly remember — 啊，对了，张东给你打电话了没有？
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 对了 mid-conversation to shift to a remembered point. Not ‘correct’ here.

example.zh: 啊，对了，张东给你打电话了没有？
example.pinyin: A, duìle, Zhāng Dōng gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà le méiyǒu?
example.en: Oh — by the way, did Zhang Dong call you?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 忘 like the word you’ll use when you left the phone off — 我忘开机了.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 忘 + verb/noun. 课文 pairs 忘开机了.

example.pinyin: A! Duìle, wǒ wàng kāijī le.
example.en: Ah! Right — I forgot to turn my phone back on.

words.en: to turn on one’s mobile phone
words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 开机 like the opposite of 关机 — power the phone on.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 开机 for phones and computers. Related 开 is under this entry.

example.pinyin: Wǒ wàng kāijī le.
example.en: I forgot to turn the phone on.

words.en: to turn on; to switch on
words.note: Listed under the numbered shengci entry in the book (related form). Headword pinyin printed. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 开 like the switch-on half of 开机.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 开 devices and doors. Here it is the 开 in 开机.

example.pinyin: Wǒ wàng kāijī le.
example.en: I forgot to turn the phone on.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added. Grammar contrast with 再 is in this lesson.
words.when: Remember 又 like the ‘again’ for something that already repeated — 电话又响了, 又输了.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 又 for a repeated past/present action; 再 for a future repeat (see 语法).

example.zh: 快！电话又响了，你去接吧。
example.pinyin: Kuài! Diànhuà yòu xiǎng le, nǐ qù jiē ba.
example.en: Quick — the phone’s ringing again; go answer it.

words.en: to make a sound; to ring
words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 响 like the word you’ll use when the phone rings — 电话又响了.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 电话响了 / 闹钟响了. Here the second call comes in.

example.zh: 快！电话又响了，你去接吧。
example.pinyin: Kuài! Diànhuà yòu xiǎng le, nǐ qù jiē ba.
example.en: Quick — the phone’s ringing again; go answer it.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 接 like the word you’ll use for answering a call — 你去接吧, 接电话.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 接电话 for picking up. Also 接到 for receiving generally.

example.zh: 快！电话又响了，你去接吧。
example.pinyin: Kuài! Diànhuà yòu xiǎng le, nǐ qù jiē ba.
example.en: Quick — the phone’s ringing again; go answer it.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 踢 like the verb in 踢足球 — go play soccer.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 踢足球 / 踢球. 课文：我去踢足球了.

example.pinyin: Wǒ qù tī zúqiú le.
example.en: I went to play soccer.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 比赛 like the match itself — 跟留学生代表队比赛了.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 比赛 as noun or verb for a contest. Here the team played a game.

example.zh: 今天我们跟留学生代表队比赛了。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen gēn liúxuéshēng dàibiǎoduì bǐsài le.
example.en: Today we played against the international-student team.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 队 like the squad — 你们队又输了吧？
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers name sports sides 队 (足球队, 代表队). 课文 asks if 你们队 lost again.

example.pinyin: Nǐmen duì yòu shū le ba?
example.en: Your team lost again, right?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 输 like the opposite of 赢 — lose the match.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 输了 for losing a game. 田芳 assumes they lost again.

example.pinyin: Nǐmen duì yòu shū le ba?
example.en: Your team lost again, right?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 赢 like the good result — 这次我们赢了.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 赢了 for winning. 张东 corrects: this time they won.

example.pinyin: Méiyǒu. Zhè cì wǒmen yíng le.
example.en: No. This time we won.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added. Book gloss: (in a score) to.
words.when: Remember 比 like the score link — 几比几？二比一.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers read scores as A比B (二比一 = 2–1). Not the comparison 比 here.

example.pinyin: Jǐ bǐ jǐ?
example.en: What was the score?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 祝贺 like the cheer after a win — 祝贺你们！
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 祝贺 + person for congratulations. 田芳 congratulates the team.

example.pinyin: Zhùhè nǐmen!
example.en: Congratulations!

words.en: an interjection used as a reminder
words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 哎 like the soft ‘hey / so…’ before a new ask — 哎，你有什么事儿吗？
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 哎 to catch attention or shift topic. Here 田芳 pivots to why he called.

example.pinyin: Āi, nǐ yǒu shénme shìr ma?
example.en: Hey — what’s up? Do you need something?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 上 like attending a course — 上托福班.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 上课 / 上班 / 上…班 for attending. Here: TOEFL class.

example.pinyin: Nǐ bú shì yào shàng Tuōfú bān ma?
example.en: Didn’t you want to attend a TOEFL class?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 托福 like the exam name — 托福班, 考托福.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers keep 托福 as the proper name for TOEFL. Capitalize in English gloss.

example.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì yě xiǎng kǎo Tuōfú?
example.en: Do you also want to take the TOEFL?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 已经 like ‘already done’ — 已经报了.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers put 已经 before the verb for completed/prior action. 田芳已经报了名.

example.pinyin: Yǐjīng bào le.
example.en: I’ve already registered.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 考 like sitting an exam — 考托福.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 考 + exam name. Related 考试 appears in 补充生词 (not listed here).

example.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì yě xiǎng kǎo Tuōfú?
example.en: Do you also want to take the TOEFL?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 陪 like coming along with someone — 你陪我一起去.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 陪 someone to a place. 张东 asks 田芳 to go register with him.

example.zh: 我想明天去报名，你陪我一起去，好吗？
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng míngtiān qù bàomíng, nǐ péi wǒ yìqǐ qù, hǎo ma?
example.en: I want to go register tomorrow — will you come with me?

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.pinyin: Wèi, shì Tián Fāng ma?
lines.en: Hello — is that Tian Fang?

lines.speaker: 田芳妈
lines.pinyin: Tián Fāng bú zài. Shì Zhāng Dōng ba?
lines.en: Tian Fang isn’t here. Is this Zhang Dong?

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.zh: 阿姨，您好！田芳去哪儿了？
lines.pinyin: Āyí, nín hǎo! Tián Fāng qù nǎr le?
lines.en: Auntie, hello! Where has Tian Fang gone?

lines.speaker: 田芳妈
lines.zh: 她四点多就去同学家了。她的一个中学同学要出国，她去看看她。
lines.pinyin: Tā sì diǎn duō jiù qù tóngxué jiā le. Tā de yí ge zhōngxué tóngxué yào chūguó, tā qù kànkan tā.
lines.en: She left for a classmate’s place after four. One of her middle-school classmates is going abroad, so she went to see her.

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.pinyin: Tā shénme shíhou néng huílai?
lines.en: When can she come back?

lines.speaker: 田芳妈
lines.zh: 她没说，你打她的手机吧。
lines.pinyin: Tā méi shuō, nǐ dǎ tā de shǒujī ba.
lines.en: She didn’t say — why don’t you call her mobile.

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.pinyin: Wǒ dǎ le, kěshì tā guānjī le.
lines.en: I called, but her phone was off.

lines.speaker: 田芳妈
lines.zh: 是吗？你过一会儿再打吧。
lines.pinyin: Shì ma? Nǐ guò yíhuìr zài dǎ ba.
lines.en: Is that so? Try again in a little while.

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.pinyin: Āyí, Tián Fāng huílai le méiyǒu?
lines.en: Auntie — has Tian Fang come back yet?

lines.speaker: 田芳妈
lines.pinyin: Hái méiyǒu ne.
lines.en: Not yet.

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.pinyin: Mā, wǒ huílai le.
lines.en: Mom, I’m back.

lines.speaker: 田芳妈
lines.zh: 饿了吧？快吃饭吧！啊，对了，张东给你打电话了没有？
lines.pinyin: È le ba? Kuài chī fàn ba! A, duìle, Zhāng Dōng gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà le méiyǒu?
lines.en: Hungry, right? Come eat! Oh — by the way, did Zhang Dong call you?

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.pinyin: Méiyǒu a.
lines.en: No.

lines.speaker: 田芳妈
lines.zh: 他来电话找你，说打你的手机，你关机了。
lines.pinyin: Tā lái diànhuà zhǎo nǐ, shuō dǎ nǐ de shǒujī, nǐ guānjī le.
lines.en: He called looking for you — said he tried your mobile and it was off.

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.pinyin: A! Duìle, wǒ wàng kāijī le.
lines.en: Ah! Right — I forgot to turn my phone back on.

lines.speaker: 田芳妈
lines.zh: 快！电话又响了，你去接吧。
lines.pinyin: Kuài! Diànhuà yòu xiǎng le, nǐ qù jiē ba.
lines.en: Quick — the phone’s ringing again; go answer it.

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.zh: 喂，张东，下午你给我打电话了吧？
lines.pinyin: Wèi, Zhāng Dōng, xiàwǔ nǐ gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà le ba?
lines.en: Hello, Zhang Dong — you called me this afternoon, right?

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.pinyin: Dǎ le, nǐ zěnme guānjī le?
lines.en: I did — why was your phone off?

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.zh: 对不起，我忘开机了。下午你做什么了？
lines.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ wàng kāijī le. Xiàwǔ nǐ zuò shénme le?
lines.en: Sorry — I forgot to turn it on. What did you do this afternoon?

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.zh: 我去踢足球了。今天我们跟留学生代表队比赛了。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ qù tī zúqiú le. Jīntiān wǒmen gēn liúxuéshēng dàibiǎoduì bǐsài le.
lines.en: I went to play soccer. Today we played against the international-student team.

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.pinyin: Nǐmen duì yòu shū le ba?
lines.en: Your team lost again, right?

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.pinyin: Méiyǒu. Zhè cì wǒmen yíng le.
lines.en: No. This time we won.

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.pinyin: Jǐ bǐ jǐ?
lines.en: What was the score?

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.pinyin: Èr bǐ yī.
lines.en: Two to one.

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.zh: 祝贺你们！哎，你有什么事儿吗？
lines.pinyin: Zhùhè nǐmen! Āi, nǐ yǒu shénme shìr ma?
lines.en: Congratulations! Hey — what’s up? Do you need something?

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.zh: 我想问问你，你不是要上托福班吗？报名了没有？
lines.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng wènwen nǐ, nǐ bú shì yào shàng Tuōfú bān ma? Bàomíng le méiyǒu?
lines.en: I wanted to ask — didn’t you want to attend a TOEFL class? Have you registered?

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.zh: 已经报了。你是不是也想考托福？
lines.pinyin: Yǐjīng bào le. Nǐ shì bu shì yě xiǎng kǎo Tuōfú?
lines.en: I’ve already registered. Do you also want to take the TOEFL?

lines.speaker: 张东
lines.zh: 是。我想明天去报名，你陪我一起去，好吗？
lines.pinyin: Shì. Wǒ xiǎng míngtiān qù bàomíng, nǐ péi wǒ yìqǐ qù, hǎo ma?
lines.en: Yes. I want to go register tomorrow — will you come with me?

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.pinyin: Hǎo de.
lines.en: Okay.

notes.title: 下午你给我打电话了吧？
notes.body: 语气助词“吧”在这里表示疑问的语气。The modal particle “吧” is used here to express an inquisitive tone. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added.

example.zh: 下午你给我打电话了吧？
example.pinyin: Xiàwǔ nǐ gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà le ba?
example.en: You called me this afternoon, right?

notes.title: 你不是要上托福班吗？
notes.body: “不是……吗？”是个反问句，强调肯定。不要求回答。“不是……吗” is a rhetorical question emphasizing the affirmative tone; therefore, no reply is required. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added.

example.pinyin: Nǐ bú shì yào shàng Tuōfú bān ma?
example.en: Didn’t you want to attend a TOEFL class?

notes.title: 你是不是也想考托福？
notes.body: 在用“是不是”的正反问句里，“是不是”可以用在谓语前，也可用在句首或句尾。In an affirmative-negative question, “是不是” can be used before the predicate or at the beginning or end of the sentence. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added.

example.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì xiǎng jiā le?
example.en: Are you homesick?

notes.title: 语气助词“了”（1）
notes.body: 语气助词“了”用在句尾，表示肯定的语气，有成句的作用。说明事情的发生、动作的完成、情况的出现和状态的变化等。正反问：……了+没有？“还没（有）……呢”表示事件现在还没有开始或完成，含有即将开始或完成的意思。注意：动词前用“没（有）”否定时句末不能用“了”；表达经常性动作时句末也不能用“了”。Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added.

example.pinyin: Tián Fāng de shǒujī guānjī le.
example.en: Tian Fang’s phone was turned off.

notes.title: “再”和“又”
notes.body: 副词“再”和“又”都可以放在动词前边作状语，表示动作或情况的重复。不同的是：“再”用于表示尚未重复的动作或情况；“又”一般用来表示已经重复的动作或情况。Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added.

example.zh: 今天我去看她了，明天我想再去。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ qù kàn tā le, míngtiān wǒ xiǎng zài qù.
example.en: I went to see her today; tomorrow I want to go again.
